prompt:
A pneumatic ram pushes a carriage along a horizontal testing track. High-pressure gas inside the cylinder expands against the piston as the carriage moves over a total stroke of 0.80 m.
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Two-part diagram. (a) Graph of force F / N against displacement s / m for 0 <= s <= 0.80 m. Force starts at 500 N at s = 0, decreases linearly to 200 N at s = 0.50 m, then remains constant at 200 N from s = 0.50 m to s = 0.80 m. (b) Schematic diagram of pneumatic cylinder with piston cross-sectional area 2.5 * 10^-3 m^2.]
(a) Determine the work done by the gas on the piston:
(i) between s = 0 and s = 0.50 m. [2]
(ii) between s = 0.50 m and s = 0.80 m. [1]
(iii) during the complete 0.80 m displacement. [1]
(b) The circular piston has a cross-sectional area of 2.5 * 10^-3 m^2.
(i) Calculate the change in volume Delta V of the gas during the constant-force stage (from s = 0.50 m to s = 0.80 m). [1]
(ii) Calculate the gas pressure inside the cylinder during this constant-force stage. [1]

parts.description: Calculate work from trapezium area under linear force curve
Calculate work from rectangular area under constant force
Sum total work done over full stroke
Calculate volume change from area and displacement
Calculate gas pressure during constant-force expansion

part_enrichment.guidance: Award M1 for trapezium formula 0.5 * (500 + 200) * 0.50, A1 for 175 J.
part_enrichment.common_pitfalls: Using rectangle of height 500 N instead of averaging force over linear decrease.
Multiplying 200 by 0.80 instead of the 0.30 m interval.
Arithmetic slips when combining parts (i) and (ii).

part_enrichment.guidance: Award A1 for Delta V = A * Delta s = 2.5 * 10^-3 * 0.30 = 7.5 * 10^-4 m^3.
part_enrichment.common_pitfalls: Using total stroke 0.80 m instead of Delta s = 0.30 m.
Dividing work by area instead of force by area.

hints: In (a)(i), treat the region as a trapezium or split into a rectangle and triangle.
In (a)(ii), the base is 0.80 m - 0.50 m = 0.30 m.
In (b)(i), change in volume is cross-sectional area multiplied by displacement.
In (b)(ii), pressure is force divided by cross-sectional area.
teacher_walkthrough: Integrates graphical work determination with microscopic piston thermodynamics.
Shows two equivalent paths for part (b)(ii): p = F/A and p = W / Delta V.
Confirms consistency of mechanical and thermodynamic definitions of work done.

provenance.abstract_pattern: combined force-displacement graphical area and thermodynamic expansion
provenance.independence_statement: Authored as an original multipart question bridging graphical force curves with cylinder gas expansion.
